slot.brief: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field at an oblique angle; ask to show/identify that the path is a helix and find its pitch or radius (easy direct formula).

stem: A charged particle with specific charge q/m = 10^8 C kg^-1 moves with velocity 6 x 10^6 m s^-1 and enters a uniform magnetic field of 0.3 T at an angle of 30 degrees with the field. The radius of the helical path traced by the particle is

verdicts.working: The perpendicular speed is v⊥ = 6×10⁶ sin 30° = 3×10⁶ m s⁻¹. Thus r = v⊥/[(q/m)B] = 3×10⁶/(10⁸×0.3) = 0.10 m = 10 cm.

working:
Helical radius r = v sin(theta) / ((q/m) B). Here v sin(30 degrees) = 6 x 10^6 * 0.5 = 3 x 10^6 m s^-1 and (q/m) B = 10^8 * 0.3 = 3 x 10^7. So r = (3 x 10^6)/(3 x 10^7) = 0.1 m = 10 cm. Correct option is B.

Independent check: The perpendicular speed is v⊥ = 6×10⁶ sin 30° = 3×10⁶ m s⁻¹. Thus r = v⊥/[(q/m)B] = 3×10⁶/(10⁸×0.3) = 0.10 m = 10 cm.
solution:
The helical radius is determined by the velocity component perpendicular to the field:
$$r=\frac{v\sin\theta}{(q/m)B}=\frac{6\times10^6\sin30^\circ}{10^8\times0.3}=0.10\,\text{m}=10\,\text{cm}.$$
